cards.text: The Teacher, son of David and king in Jerusalem (Ecclesiastes 1:1), is still working out how life goes under the sun. Now he opens with a question: "Who is like the wise man? Who knows the interpretation of a matter?" Friend, I once spent a whole week in that junk drawer trying to interpret a twist tie, so I'm listening.

cards.question: The Teacher says a man's wisdom does something to his face. What does it do?

cards.text: Then the Teacher gets practical for anyone serving a king: keep the king's command. Not "I'll think about it." Not "let's circle back Monday." KEEP it.

cards.question: The Teacher says to keep the king's command. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Because of your oath before God
Because the king pays your wages
Because the people are watching you

cards.text: Next tip: don't hurry out of the king's presence, and don't keep pushing a bad cause. You know the guy in the meeting who already lost the argument and raises his hand AGAIN? Don't be that guy in a throne room.

cards.question: Why does the Teacher say not to keep pushing a bad cause in front of the king?

answers.text: He will do whatever he pleases
He only listens to his advisers

cards.question: Since the king does whatever he pleases, the Teacher says anyone can walk right up and ask him, "What are you doing?"
The Teacher says whoever keeps the king's command will come to no harm.
The Teacher says a wise heart knows the right ___ and procedure.

cards.text: The Teacher says there's a right time and procedure to every purpose, even when a man's misery weighs heavily on him. It's like my oven, friend: a minute early is raw dough, a minute late is a hockey puck.

cards.question: Right after talking about timing, the Teacher says a wise man can always tell people what is to come.

cards.text: Then the Teacher lines up things nobody controls, starting with this: no man has power over the wind to contain it. I've watched one little breeze chase a stack of parchment clear across my bakery, and all I could do was wave my mustache at it.

cards.question: No one can hold back the wind. What else does the Teacher say no one has authority over?
As no one can be discharged in wartime, so ___ will not release those who practice it.

cards.text: The Teacher says he's seen all this, putting his mind to every deed done under the sun. He's seen a time when one man lords it over another, to his own detriment. Friend, we've ALL had that boss.
Then the Teacher watches a burial. The ones being buried are wicked people who used to go in and out of the holy place.

cards.question: What happens to these wicked people in the city where they went in and out of the holy place?

cards.text: His verdict: "This too is futile." Then he notices what happens when the sentence for a crime drags its feet, like the office where nobody ever checks who's late, so pretty soon NOBODY shows up on time.

cards.question: When the sentence for a crime is not carried out quickly, what does the Teacher say happens to people's hearts?

answers.text: They become fully set on doing evil
They grow more afraid of the judge
They learn to forgive one another

cards.text: A sinner can do evil a hundred times and still live long. A HUNDRED times! I stamped a few blurry cookies and got sent to the back of a drawer.

cards.question: Even so, the Teacher says he knows it will go well with those who ___ God and are reverent in His presence.
The Teacher says that because the wicked do not fear God, their days will lengthen like a shadow.

cards.text: Then the Teacher spots another futility done on the earth. And friend, this one sends my eyebrows all the way up into my chef's hat.

cards.question: What does the Teacher see happening to some righteous men on the earth?

answers.text: They get what the wicked deserve
They get double the reward they earned
They get honored by the king

cards.question: The Teacher also sees some wicked men getting what the actions of the righteous deserve.

cards.text: So after all that futility, where does the Teacher land? Somewhere I did NOT see coming.

cards.question: After seeing all this futility, what does the Teacher commend?

cards.text: There's nothing better for a man under the sun, he says, than to eat and drink and be merry. Friend, I've been saying that over a warm batch for YEARS.

cards.question: The Teacher says this joy will go with a man in his ___ during the days of his life that ___ gives him under the sun.

cards.text: Then the Teacher puts his mind to knowing wisdom and watches people work so hard their eyes don't see sleep, day or night. I know that look. That's me staring at the oven timer at three in the morning.

cards.question: After seeing every work of God, what does the Teacher say a man can do with the work done under the sun?

answers.text: He is unable to comprehend it
He can master it with effort
He can explain it to others

cards.question: The Teacher says that when a wise man claims to know the meaning of the work under the sun, he truly comprehends it.
